job: Choose a plan and see what every call will cost before signing up.
purpose: The pricing page of Ember's public site: a short type-led head, four plans in columns with a monthly or yearly switch, a comparison table that shows one plan at a time on a phone, usage prices per endpoint as rows, questions about credits beside their head, and an inset offer to move a crawl. No logos and no figures: the prices are the page. ?state=yearly opens it with yearly prices.
useWhen: Visitors compare plans and want the price of each call.
Plans differ in more ways than a plan column can list.

avoidWhen.when: The visitor does not yet know what the product does.
A signed-in team changes its plan or reads its bill.
A signed-in team reads what it has used.

sections.why: The same bar as the home: pricing is the next page most visitors open.
A short head; the plans right under it are the picture, so no media.
Four plans read side by side, with the period switch above them.
The plans differ in more than five ways; the table carries what the columns leave out.
Usage is priced per endpoint: seven lines read down, not across.
The head and a person to write to stay beside the answers.
An inset offer for teams moving from their own scrapers; the page's one texture.
Pricing readers look for terms, the DPA and status, so every link column is there.

states.name: monthly
states.how: the default: the segmented control on Monthly

states.name: yearly
